blocks.content: The Armed Forces Tribunal was established under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007 to adjudicate service matters and court-martial appeals.

rows: Governed by respective force acts and regular courts

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) was established under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007, and formally inaugurated in August 2009.
It consists of a Judicial Member (a retired Supreme Court Judge or retired High Court Chief Justice) and Administrative Members with military experience.
The tribunal possesses both original jurisdiction over service matters and appellate jurisdiction over court-martial orders.
Jurisdiction covers members of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, but specifically excludes Paramilitary forces such as BSF, CRPF, and Coast Guard.
Appeals against the orders and decisions of the Armed Forces Tribunal can be preferred directly before the Supreme Court of India.
Paramilitary forces like BSF, CRPF, ITBP, Assam Rifles, and Coast Guard do NOT come under the jurisdiction of the Armed Forces Tribunal.
The Chairperson of the AFT must be a retired Supreme Court Judge or a retired Chief Justice of a High Court.
The AFT exercises both Original Jurisdiction (service disputes) and Appellate Jurisdiction (court-martial verdicts).
